pages._note: Segment list as a declarative type:index page (marketing-segments-ui-repair, pipelinq#773). Add and the row Edit action open SegmentFormDialog in the form-dialog slot, which mounts SegmentBuilder, a recursive rule-tree editor rather than a declarative form. Rows have no detail page, so selection is off and a row click does nothing.

pages._note: Marketing blast list as a declarative type:index page (pipelinq-declarative-pages-round1). A row click and the built-in View open the live monitor (BlastMonitor, via rowRoute); Add opens BlastWizardDialog in the form-dialog slot: a multi-step wizard with a compliance gate (conditional advancing, an optional A/B split, template validation and a consent preflight that holds the create back pending the marketer's decision), which no declarative form expresses. Selection is off: there are no bulk actions.
pages.title: Blasts

pages._note: PerformanceDashboard.vue stays a custom page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative kept-custom). It is a three-tab post-send analytics surface (Overview / A/B testing / Attribution), not a KPI dashboard: there are no headline metrics to lift into endpoint stat widgets, and the entire body is interactive tabbed content the declarative type:dashboard cannot express. Tab 2 computes a 2x2 chi-square p-value (analytic erfc survival fn) over click rates CLIENT-SIDE per A/B pair and gates the verdict on >=500 delivered + 24h elapsed; Tab 3 does an N+1 fan-out (one GET /api/blasts/:id/attribution per blast) and sums attributed deals/EUR; Tab 1 is a client-sortable table over blast totals with an id->name segment lookup. Missing primitives: (1) a tab-container body primitive (a dashboard cannot host a role=tablist switcher); (2) a client-side derived/statistical widget source (the chi-square significance verdict is not an endpoint scalar); (3) an N+1 per-row enrichment fetch (attribution is one request per listed blast, not a single aggregation endpoint).
pages.title: Blast performance
Blast monitor
pages._note: Declarative pages render a snapshot; this one is live. It owns a polling lifecycle (startPolling / stopPolling / clearInterval on unmount) and derives send progress from it — progressPercent, processed, audienceTotal, etaLabel and a buildTimeline series — plus an in-flight cancel action guarded by canCancel. There is no declarative primitive for a page that must keep refetching and be torn down cleanly.
